subject: E function
notes: Verdict SURVIVES; the note is corrected and the SPEC BASIS the adjudicator missed is supplied. test-needed. Citations re-validated: cite.py --check 15.27.3 'standard-binary arithmetic is in effect' -> OK (rule 2). THE PRECONDITION CAN NEVER HOLD IN THIS COMPILER, re-verified by me on the built CLI: DataBinder.BindDeclarations rejects the mode with COBOL0806 'ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is an obsolete feature (ISO 8.8.1.4.1 NOTE 1 / Annex F) and is not supported; use NATIVE or STANDARD-DECIMAL' - a HARD error at --std 2002 (alongside COBOL0900 'requires COBOL-2014'), 2014 and 2023, and NOT downgradable by --permissive (2023 adds the COBOL0903 obsolescence warning and still errors). Nothing in the tree computes 14114126198520207781233383725636853 / (2 ** 112); CobolIntrinsics.E() is the only body and is Math.E in every mode. WHAT THE ADJUDICATOR MISSED, and it is what makes this an owner DECISION rather than a bug: the standard itself classes this clause as processor-dependent. Annex A.3 item 2, validated verbatim - cite.py --check A.3 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' -> OK - and 4.5 NOTE, validated verbatim ('These factors can include the use of optional, processor-dependent, or implementor-defined language elements'), together mean a conforming implementation may fail to translate a compilation group that uses it without ceasing to conform. Annex F.2 additionally makes STANDARD-BINARY an obsolete feature, and it is F.2 ITEM 3 - not Annex E - that records the non-implementation: '3. STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item. These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' (cite.py --check F.2 'STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item' -> OK). CITATION REPAIRED 2026-08-31, and the error was worse than a wrong annex letter: the sentence as previously quoted here ('it has not been implemented ... by any COBOL provider', singular) is F.2 ITEM 5's, which is about the VALIDATE FACILITY - a real clause answering a different question (feedback_a_real_clause_can_answer_a_different_question). Item 3 also carries the reevaluation note that makes the decline REVISITABLE: 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). The non-support is already recorded at docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 2 row 2 ('| 2 | ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY | 11.9.5 | Not claimed | Obsolete feature (A.3 NOTE 1); the native/standard-decimal modes are provided |') - the DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT shape, a verdict only the owner may set, hence NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION. BARE QUESTION: should 15.27.3 rule 2 be recorded as discharged by the existing documented non-support of ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY (Annex A.3 item 2 processor-dependence) rather than carried as an open inventory GAP? Identical to the already-adjudicated sibling RV-15.73.3-2 for PI; one decision should settle the whole 15.4.1 family. EDITIONS DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY OF INTRINSICCATALOG: the STANDARD-BINARY keyword of the ARITHMETIC clause is a COBOL-2014 addition (the 2002 clause offered NATIVE and STANDARD only; the compiler's own edition gate agrees - 'OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY.' at --std 2002 draws COBOL0900 'requires COBOL-2014 (targeting COBOL-2002)', re-run by me), so the rule's precondition cannot arise at 85 or 2002. TEST COVERAGE: none - no test references FUNCTION E under any arithmetic mode. The honest cover is a negative case pinning that FUNCTION E under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is refused BY MODE; a mode-only rejection test that never names E would not cover this row. || DERIVED VERDICT from the ONE owner determination (kb/Work PB198; owner protocol 2026-08-30, survey unanimous): ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY IS DECLINED, so a rule conditioned SOLELY on that mode is unreachable and its verdict follows mechanically rather than being adjudicated row by row. THE GROUND IS PROCESSOR-DEPENDENCE, NOT OBSOLESCENCE. Annex A.3 item 2: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK, item 2), and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support, plus the duty to warn at compile time and to document the absence ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK). Obsolescence grants NOTHING here: Annex F.2's own preamble says 'A conforming implementation shall support obsolete language elements EXCEPT for elements that are also optional or processor-dependent' (--check -> OK), so it is the processor-dependence that licenses the decline and the obsolescence is merely corroborating. REVISITABLE, by the standard's own words: F.2 item 3 ('STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item. These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' -> --check OK) adds 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). THE SCREEN, MEASURED AND FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE SET: the decline moved from DataBinder to OptionsBinder.ArithmeticOf, the single point every unit kind's OPTIONS clause is read through - DataBinder never saw a METHOD's or an INTERFACE's paragraph, so those two arms drew NO diagnostic at all at --std 2014 (kb/Work PB197). All seven unit kinds now draw exactly one COBOL0806, and ArithmeticModeScreenDriftTests reads the options-bearing productions OUT OF THE GRAMMAR so a new one cannot be added unscreened. Per-edition diagnostics are pinned with their ABSENCES too: 2002 -> 0900 + 0806, 2014 -> 0806 alone, 2023 -> 0806 + 0903. SELECTION IS DERIVED, NOT LISTED: inventory-schema.json's derived-verdicts.standard-binary-only carries the predicate as DATA, read by both the batch generator and the C# drift test, and the drift test holds every selected row at this verdict so the population cannot drift back into the four states it carried before (NOT-IMPLEMENTED 3, blank 2, NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION 4, CONFORMS 1).
